summary.text: Jacqui Irwin is the Democratic nominee for California's 26th Congressional District, an open seat. A systems engineer by training, she served on the Thousand Oaks City Council, including two terms as mayor, before her 2014 election to the California State Assembly, where she currently represents the 42nd District. She launched her congressional campaign in January 2026 after Rep. Julia Brownley announced her retirement.

paragraphs.text: Irwin was born in Woodland Hills, California, and graduated from Taft High School there before earning a bachelor of science in systems engineering from the University of California, San Diego, in 1985.
Her campaign biography adds that she was an All-American swimmer at UC San Diego.
She worked as an engineer at Teledyne Systems and at Johns Hopkins University's Applied Physics Lab.
Irwin served on the Thousand Oaks Planning Commission and was elected to the Thousand Oaks City Council in 2004.
She later served two terms as mayor of Thousand Oaks.
In 2014 she was elected to the California State Assembly from the 44th District, defeating Republican Rob McCoy 52.3% to 47.7%.
She was re-elected in 2016, 2018 and 2020, and in 2022 won election in the redrawn 42nd District.
In the Assembly, Irwin chairs the Climate Change Policies Committee, and her campaign says she also chairs the Assembly Select Committee on Cybersecurity.

She announced her candidacy for the 26th Congressional District on January 8, 2026, hours after Rep. Julia Brownley said she would not seek another term, and she advanced from the June 2 primary with 41.3% of the vote.
Irwin and her husband, Jon, have lived in Thousand Oaks for nearly 20 years, and she describes herself as the mother of three young adults.
